title: Gradual Fidelity KV Compression Playbook for Continuous Batching and GPU Memory Optimization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: establish a safe, pragmatic playbook for progressively applying lossy compression to KV caches (FP8 / INT8 / INT4 tiers) with continuous-batching workloads. We want to reduce GPU working set and enable higher effective batch concurrency while bounding user-visible quality regressions and ensuring automated rollback/fallback at runtime. This ticket covers experiment design, runtime guardrails, monitoring thresholds, and a staged rollout procedure across model families and hardware classes.
acceptance_criteria: Define per-cohort fidelity ladder (FP32->FP8->INT8->INT4) with deterministic fallback rules for token-cohort quality budgets
Implement lightweight runtime hooks to mark cache entries with fidelity metadata and attach age/priority scores for eviction and downcast decisions

Run controlled A/B experiments on synthetic and live-sampled traffic demonstrating >=18% GPU working-set reduction on A100/H100 while keeping relative generation-quality degradation <= 2 BLEU/ROUGE points or <= 1.5% perplexity delta on evaluation prompts
Automated rollback triggers: if real-time QA metrics cross thresholds (see monitoring_alerts) then automatically restore higher-fidelity cache entries for affected cohorts
Document playbook and runbook so SRE/Platform can invoke emergency fallback and interpret alerts
experiment_steps: 1) Instrument: add per-entry fidelity tags and versioned schema to KV cache metadata (small header, few bytes) and expose sampling API to snapshot entries

2) Offline sims: take representative KV snapshots from 3 model families (medium/large/llama-like) and simulate downcasting to FP8/INT8/INT4 with error injection to estimate reconstruction noise and distributional drift

3) Microbench: run generation tests in an isolated cluster using continuous batching with target batch windows (8ms, 20ms, 50ms) to measure throughput/latency trade-offs with different cache fidelity mixes
4) Cohort A/B: rollout to 5% of traffic grouped by token-cohort (short vs long contexts, interactive vs background), compare metrics to control group over 72h
5) Gradual expansion: if gates pass, expand to 20% and then to 50% while monitoring QA and tail latency; maintain ability to pin cohorts to higher fidelity
6) Postmortem: capture regressions, false positives/negatives of rollback heuristics, and memory savings per model/hardware
metrics: GPU working-set reduction (percent of KV bytes saved)
End-to-end p99 latency and median latency under continuous batching profiles
Generation quality: perplexity delta, token-level error rate, BLEU/ROUGE on eval prompts, and hallucination flag rate from safety heuristics
Token churn and cache hit ratio changes (prefix hit rate)
Fallback frequency and time-to-recovery after automated rollback
Cost-per-token inference delta (estimated GPU seconds saved)
SLO breach count and user-facing error rate after changes
hardware_matrix: A100 80GB: baseline for current production; expected moderate wins with INT8/FP8
H100 80GB: validate kernel FP8 paths and measure quantized kernel tail latency
RTX6000-class (32GB): quantify memory wins enabling slightly larger batch windows
CPU-hosted sim nodes: for offline degradation modeling and fast iteration
rollout_plan: Canary: non-critical internal tenant routes, 5% traffic, monitor 24h
Stage: increase to 20% for 72h if no quality or latency regressions beyond thresholds
Ramp: 50% with cohort-aware pinning; avoid latency spikes during peak hours by rate-limiting conversions
GA: after 2 rolling weeks with stable metrics, enable as default for eligible model+hardware combos with opt-out per-customer flag
monitoring_alerts: Alert-01: generation_quality_degradation > 1.5% (per-cohort) sustained for 30m -> auto-rollback cohort to previous fidelity
Alert-02: p99 latency increase > 20% compared to baseline sustained for 15m -> throttle new fidelity downcasts
Alert-03: cache_hit_ratio drop > 10% -> investigate destructive eviction or token churn regressions
Alert-04: fallback_rate > 0.5% of requests in a 1h window -> create SEV ticket and pause rollout
risks: Quantization artifacts in KV can cause subtle autoregressive drift leading to rare but high-impact hallucinations
Per-token quality metrics may not capture downstream application-level failures (e.g. L2 retrieval mismatch) — need human review samples
Kernel-level FP8 support differs across drivers; inconsistent performance could make some hardware regress instead of improving
Compact header per-entry increases metadata overhead; net savings must account for that
